# s438 — Skill rewrite for getting started, building a roadmap, planning and implementing

The slicer skill (`ai.skill_text()`, committed as `skills/slicer/SKILL.md`) opens by routing the four jobs an agent arrives with: getting started, building a roadmap from the docs, planning or filing, and implementing. Its description names them, so the harness loads it for those requests.

**Findings:** owner request 2026-11-02 (release 1.18.0, helping an agent get started): decision 3, update the slicer skill so it is the most useful for getting started, building a roadmap from docs, planning and implementing (split from `ai hooks`, which is its own slice) · **Size:** S · **Trees:** ai, docs

**Not in this slice:** `ai hooks` (the next slice), prompt overrides, changes to the implement loop, the exit codes or the TRACKING block wording beyond what the routing needs, and Codex or Grok specific skill text.

## Why

Owner request 2026-11-02, decision 3: update the slicer skill so it is the most useful for getting started, building a roadmap from docs, planning and implementing. This slice is the skill half; the owner allowed splitting `ai hooks` out when the combined slice would exceed M, and it would (skill text, a settings merge and a guard command).

Today (`ai.skill_text`, ai.py ~1321-1347) the skill is the implement loop, the spec-gap rule, the exit codes, the TRACKING block, a closer, a relay sentence and a last line pointing at `slicer ai instructions --rest`. `SKILL_DESCRIPTION` (ai.py ~61) says "review a roadmap, plan work, take a slice, implement the next slice, or drive slicer". An agent asked to get started or to build a roadmap from docs gets the implement loop first, which is the wrong first step for both.
